summary:
TerraRotate AI, developed by Team TerraVyn, is an AI-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data.

The application combines historical rainfall, temperature trends, satellite vegetation imagery, local soil conditions, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities to explore climate-resilient farming strategies. Farmers can enter their location, soil type, water availability, existing crop rotation, and agricultural goals to compare three rotation strategies based on potential soil health benefits, water requirements, and climate-related risks.

The platform integrates NASA POWER climate data, supports available 2026 observations, and provides visual insights, decision reports, and a Tamil/English voice assistant to improve accessibility.

TerraRotate AI addresses the challenge by translating complex environmental data into practical, understandable insights. By helping farmers explore alternatives to resource-intensive cropping practices, the project aims to support water conservation, soil sustainability, and long-term agricultural resilience while keeping farmers' experience and local expertise central to decision-making.
details:
TerraRotate AI – Project Description

TerraRotate AI, developed by Team TerraVyn, is an agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers make informed crop rotation decisions using NASA Earth observation data, local soil conditions, and farmer priorities.

How It Works

Farmers enter their location, existing crop rotation, soil texture, water availability, planting season, and farming objectives. The application retrieves historical climate observations from NASA POWER, including rainfall and temperature trends, to help identify environmental conditions relevant to farming.

Using a rule-based crop suitability and rotation scoring system, the platform compares three crop rotation strategies, including the farmer's existing rotation. It highlights potential benefits, water requirements, soil health considerations, climate-related risks, and limitations. Farmers can explore satellite vegetation imagery and generate a decision report explaining the suggested alternatives.

The application also includes a Tamil and English voice assistant designed to make agricultural information more accessible.

Technologies Used

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • NASA Data: NASA POWER API for climate observations and MODIS vegetation imagery through NASA GIBS.
  • Additional NASA Resources: SMAP, GPM, and Landsat datasets identified for future analytical integration.
  • Decision Engine: Rule-based crop rotation evaluation using farm conditions, crop characteristics, and farmer priorities.
  • Development and Deployment: Visual Studio Code, GitHub, and Vercel.
  • Voice Interface: Browser-based speech recognition and text-to-speech for Tamil and English.

The current prototype is software-based and does not require physical hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

TerraRotate AI goes beyond displaying weather information by connecting historical environmental observations with practical crop rotation decisions. Its interactive simulator enables farmers to compare different agricultural strategies instead of receiving a single fixed recommendation.

A key innovation is its farmer-centered approach: farmers' priorities, such as conserving water, improving soil health, or increasing income potential, influence how alternatives are evaluated. The bilingual voice assistant further supports accessibility for farmers who may be less comfortable with technical dashboards.

Benefits and Intended Impact

TerraRotate AI aims to help farmers identify opportunities to conserve irrigation water, support soil fertility, reduce climate-related agricultural risks, and explore more sustainable cropping practices.

The initial demonstration focuses on Tamil Nadu, India, with the potential to adapt the approach to other agricultural regions.

Factors Considered

The project considers rainfall variability, temperature trends, seasonal suitability, soil texture, water availability, crop characteristics, nitrogen-fixing potential, and farmers' economic and environmental priorities.

The prototype uses preliminary suitability scores rather than scientifically validated yield predictions. Satellite observations also have spatial and temporal limitations, and some NASA datasets are currently available as supporting resources rather than integrated scoring inputs.

TerraRotate AI is intended to support, not replace, farmers' experience and local agricultural expertise. Its long-term vision is to make Earth observation data understandable, accessible, and useful for building more climate-resilient farming communities.
